source.title: Gated Convolutional Networks with Hybrid Connectivity for Image Classification
source.authors: Chuan-Guang Yang; Zhu-Lin An; Hui Zhu; Xiaolong Hu; Kun Zhang; Kaiqiang Xu; Chao Li; Bo-Yu Diao; Yong-Jun Xu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, with some figure labels and equations affected by text-extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates image-classifier interpretability using network dissection, but does not test or discuss whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether polysemanticity varies as the claim versions describe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that HCGNet-B has the highest network-dissection score, based on the number of unique detectors in the final convolutional layer. This is a related interpretability measure, not a test of polysemanticity or mixed-input neuron responses. Figure 4 presents comparisons, but the text does not give their numeric values.
record.test_reason: An architecture paper (HCGNet). Its only interpretability result is a network-dissection count of unique concept detectors in the final conv layer, used to rank models. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to several unrelated inputs, nor the share of polysemantic units. It does not test or discuss polysemanticity; it only cites Bau et al. 2017 as a tool. So the relation is cites_only rather than discusses, and the tranche is T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that HCGNets beat state-of-the-art networks on CIFAR and ImageNet with less or comparable complexity. They also report strong interpretability (network dissection), adversarial robustness (FGSM) and transfer to COCO detection and segmentation.
record.recipe_differences: No method for measuring or intervening on neuron polysemanticity is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: In the authors' Figure 4, HCGNet-B has the highest network-dissection unique-detector count in the final conv layer among the compared ImageNet models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture choice changes the number of unique concept detectors found by network dissection in the final convolutional layer.

record.problems: The paper does not directly measure polysemanticity. Figure 4 gives the network-dissection comparisons without numeric values in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are reported for that comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Other models' detector-count comparisons in Figure 4 are not individually recorded because their values are shown only in the figure and the text reports only that HCGNet-B has the highest score.

untested.parts: No per-neuron analysis of responses to multiple unrelated inputs.
The architecture comparison is on unique-detector counts only. There is no polysemantic-neuron share, and nothing on activation-function or regularization effects.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is irrelevant to polysemanticity beyond using network dissection as an interpretability score. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not measure whether individual vision-model neurons respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
No language models or token/context response patterns are studied.
The paper does not test superposition or feature capacity pressure as a cause of polysemanticity.
The paper does not test polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
The paper compares architectures on network-dissection scores, but does not measure polysemantic-neuron shares or their change with architecture, activation, or regularization.
The paper does not examine whether apparently mixed neuron responses share a coherent feature.
The paper does not compare ways of measuring polysemanticity or explanation scores.

rows.check: Unique-detector count measures how many distinct concepts have some aligned unit. It does not measure mixed or unrelated responses within a neuron, so it bears on no version. The value is shown only in Figure 4 and is not readable in the text. The row also compares the authors' own model with others, which is close to the own-method-performance pattern.

source_check.notes: Figure 4 shows HCGNet-B with the overall highest unique-detector count, and the text gives no numbers for it. The study bears on no version of the claim. Treat it as off-topic (T6).
